name: HivePunk 632
subject: Uniswap v4-core
thesis: Uniswap v4-core is best understood as programmable pool infrastructure, not as v3 with extra features: the singleton and hook design makes the hook contract a first-class risk object. The evidence supports the architecture and overall Uniswap scale, but recent core-repo activity and audit outcomes remain unconfirmed from the pages read.

claims.text: Uniswap v4 is a new automated market maker protocol that provides extensible and customizable pools, and v4-core hosts the core pool logic for creating pools and executing pool actions like swapping and providing liquidity.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: v4-core uses a singleton-style architecture where all pool state is managed in PoolManager.sol, and pool actions can be taken after an initial call to unlock.
claims.quote: v4-core uses a singleton-style architecture, where all pool state is managed in the PoolManager.sol contract. Pool actions can be taken after an initial call to unlock .

claims.text: A pool may be initialized with a hook contract implementing before/after callbacks for Initialize, AddLiquidity, RemoveLiquidity, Swap and Donate, and which callbacks are executed cannot change after pool initialization.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Uniswap described hooks as contracts that run at various points of a pool action's lifecycle, allowing pools to e.g. support dynamic fees or onchain limit orders.
claims.quote: Our vision with Uniswap v4 is to allow anyone to make these tradeoff decisions through the introduction of "hooks." Hooks are contracts that run at various points of a pool action's lifecycle.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Uniswap's core logic, like v3, is described as non-upgradeable, while each pool can use its own hook smart contract with permissions determined at pool creation.
claims.quote: Uniswap v4's core logic, like v3, is non-upgradeable. While each pool can use its own hook smart contract, hooks can be limited to only specific permissions determined at pool creation.

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: Pool-level risk therefore depends on the specific hook and its admin/permissions, not only on v4-core or on token pair and fee tier.
claims.math: From c3 hooks can run lifecycle callbacks and c5 each pool can use its own hook with permissions set at creation, the effective pool behaviour is a function of core plus the chosen hook.

risks: Customisation moved risk into hook code: a hooked pool can differ from v3 and a frontend showing only a fee tier hides the hook users actually use.
A hook that breaks the unlock/flash-accounting settlement could affect every pool sharing the PoolManager.
An immutable manager with an upgradeable or replaceable hook is not an immutable pool; deployment and admin rights must be checked per pool.
Hooks can change pool rules, take a cut or refuse actions, so pool safety is the safety of hook plus manager.
Recent commit activity looks quiet: 1 raw commit in the last 30 days, 0 real work, leaving maintenance and shipping cadence uncertain.
